messages:
alex: Heads-up — I'm opening a small Terraform change to provision a capacity-reserved GPU nodepool for inference-prod in us-west-2. Goal: stable latency for 99th pct requests during peak. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/762

maria: Nice. Are we talking full reserved (no spot) or a mixed strategy?

alex: Thinking two pools: reserved p4d for steady baseline (capacity reservation), and a spot-backed p4d-burst pool for extra throughput. Need input on taints/affinity and how autoscaler should prefer reserved.

priya: For scheduling, add a node-label like "redwood.infra/gpu-reserve=reserved" and taint reserved nodes with "dedicated=reserved:NoSchedule". Then workload spec can use nodeAffinity + toleration. Short example: 
```yaml
nodeSelector:
  redwood.infra/gpu-reserve: reserved
tolerations:
- key: "dedicated"
  operator: "Equal"
  value: "reserved"
  effect: "NoSchedule"
```
This keeps the reserved pool for latency-sensitive pods.

ken: For the autoscaler, we can set the spot ASG with lower priority scaling policy and a custom expander so Kube-Autoscaler drains/backs off to reserved first. Also we should set node-group priorities in the cluster-autoscaler flags: `--node-group-auto-discovery` + `--expander=least-waste` ??? (we should test).

maria: Also remember to set EC2 Capacity Reservations to "open" for the account or use CR group id in the Launch Template. Terraform snippet I was testing: 
```hcl
resource "aws_ec2_capacity_reservation" "p4d_reserved" {
  instance_type = "p4d.24xlarge"
  availability_zone = "us-west-2a"
  instance_platform = "Linux/UNIX"
  count = 2
  tags = { team = "inference" }
}

resource "aws_launch_template" "p4d_reserved_lt" {
  name_prefix = "p4d-reserved-"
  // user_data installs drivers and joins cluster
  capacity_reservation_specification {
    capacity_reservation_preference = "open"
  }
}
```
Note: CR API differs slightly by region; I left in PRE preference rather than pinning to a single CR id so we can reuse across AZs.

alex: Good call. We want preference=open to avoid brittle single-CR dependence. For critical pools we might create CR groups per-AZ and reference by id though.

priya: One more for secrets/drivers: the user-data needs access to the SSM param containing the driver bootstrap token. We should wire the IAM instance profile to allow ssm:GetParameter for `/inference/gpu-driver-token`. In Terraform the instance profile change is in iam.tf.

ken: Can someone add a small smoke test in cluster-qa to ensure the reserved pool handles 50 concurrent small inference pods without OOM? I can add a k8s job to spawn pods with `resources: requests: cpu: 4, nvidia.com/gpu: 1` and measure latency.

alex: I'll add the PR with the changes and the smoke job. infra-bot ran the plan already and reported no destructive changes to prod: 

infra-bot: terraform plan for branch feature/gpu-reserve: no changes to existing resources, 2 to add (aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.p4d_reserved, aws_launch_template.p4d_reserved_lt).

maria: Quick nits for PR review: please include updated docs in /docs/infra/gpu-nodepools.md that explain the label/taint pattern and how to request bursts to spot. Also add a runbook note for CR failures and fallback to on-demand.

alex: Ack — docs + runbook on the PR. If no objections I'll merge after one LGTM and schedule a staged rollout this Friday 02:00 UTC to avoid peak.

priya: LGTM from me after IAM role change is validated in staging.

ken: Will run smoke test tomorrow and report.

maria: :+1: Thanks!

alex: Thanks all — I'll tag reviewers and keep channel updated.
